answer: HYPOTHESIS (natural language, data-grounded): Across the three wealth snapshots available in this dataset — 1985, 1990, and 1996 — the median family net wealth of white individuals (proxied by the only defensible category in the data, Non-Black Non-Hispanic, cohort 3) is consistently and substantially higher than that of Black and Hispanic individuals, and this gap WIDENS over the 1985→1996 window. In complete-case per-year medians (n reported beside each): 1985 — White(proxy) $3,500 (n=5,774) vs Black $1,600 (n=1,699) vs Hispanic $500 (n=2,631); 1990 — White $12,972 (n=5,336) vs Black $4,800 (n=1,528) vs Hispanic $1,600 (n=2,431); 1996 — White $42,600 (n=3,557) vs Black $9,800 (n=1,368) vs Hispanic $2,562 (n=2,114). The White-to-Black median ratio grows from 2.2x (1985) to 2.7x (1990) to 4.3x (1996), and the White-to-Hispanic ratio from 7.0x to 8.1x to 16.6x; absolute White–Black and White–Hispanic dollar gaps also widen ($1,900→$8,172→$32,800 and $3,000→$11,372→$40,038). In every snapshot the ordering is White > Black > Hispanic, with the low Hispanic median driven in part by a large zero-wealth share (31% zero in 1985, 22% in 1996, vs 2–7% for the White proxy). This is a WIDENING gap observed across the three 1985/1990/1996 snapshots (the only wealth years in the data), not a claim of continuous annual coverage, and it is an UNWEIGHTED, sample-level result (no weight column exists), so it describes this NLSY79 sample rather than population-weighted national medians. Robustness: the balanced panel of respondents with all three wealth values (n=5,739: 1,084 Black / 1,723 Hispanic / 2,932 White-proxy) reproduces the same ordering and widening (White/Black 2.38x→4.69x; White/Hispanic 12.7x→17.8x). Zero and negative (debt) wealth values were retained as valid observations; median (not mean) is the reported metric per the question.

payload.hypothesis: Since the earliest available snapshot (1985), the median family net wealth of white (Non-Black Non-Hispanic) individuals exceeds that of Black and Hispanic individuals in every wealth year observed (1985, 1990, 1996), by a factor that WIDENS from 2.2x to 4.3x vs Black and from 7.0x to 16.6x vs Hispanic; every year the ordering is White > Black > Hispanic, with Hispanic medians lagging due to a large zero/near-zero wealth share.
payload.workflow: Read nls_raw.csv (12,686x61). Mapped cohort 1=BLACK, 2=HISPANIC, 3=Non-Black Non-Hispanic=WHITE proxy (no explicit white flag exists). Metric = median family net wealth for the three wealth snapshots (1985, 1990, 1996 — the only wealth years present). Missingness = complete-case per year (n reported for every median) with a balanced-panel (all 3 years, n=5,739) robustness run because attrition is differential (White-proxy 52.6% missing in 1996). Negative/debt and zero wealth retained as valid observations (no trimming/floored). Bootstrap 95% CIs for medians. CPI-U sensitivity (1985/1990→1996 dollars) used only for growth-over-time statements; within-year group ratios are inflation-invariant. Unweighted: no weight column exists in the data, so results describe this NLSY79 sample.
